title: Covered AI Prohibition Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: The Covered AI Prohibition Act is a proposed law that seeks to ban the use of certain artificial intelligence systems deemed “covered” under the act. It aims to curb potential risks associated with these AI technologies by imposing strict restrictions on their deployment and development.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act prohibits the construction or operation of new data centers dedicated to AI processing, aiming to curb environmental impact and regulatory concerns. It allows existing centers to continue but requires them to adopt stricter sustainability and oversight measures before the moratorium ends.

title: To direct the Director of National Intelligence to submit to Congress a report on the use of artificial intelligence systems to acquire, analyze, query, disseminate, or otherwise access information under section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978.
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The policy directs the Director of National Intelligence to deliver a report to Congress detailing how AI systems are used to collect, analyze, query, or share information under Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. This report is intended to give lawmakers oversight and ensure transparency about AI’s role in U.S. intelligence activities.

title: A bill to require entities to include human-controlled shutdown mechanisms in all artificial intelligence systems.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This bill mandates that every entity deploying artificial intelligence must build a shutdown feature that can be fully controlled by a human. It aims to ensure that people can immediately halt any AI system if it behaves unexpectedly or poses a risk.

title: To require the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disclose each instance in which the Secretary uses artificial intelligence to interact with a covered individual, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The policy requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to disclose each time artificial intelligence is used to interact with a covered individual. It also mandates disclosure of all other instances where the Secretary employs AI for official purposes.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop Rogue AI Act is a proposed law that seeks to prevent dangerous or malicious AI systems from harming people or society. It would create strict rules, safety checks, and penalties to ensure AI technologies are developed and used responsibly.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open-Source AI Leadership Act encourages the creation and sharing of AI technology through open-source platforms, aiming to make AI development more transparent, collaborative, and widely accessible. It establishes federal support, sets standards, and outlines governance to ensure that open-source AI projects remain aligned with public benefit and societal values.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: This act prohibits the construction or operation of AI data centers on federal lands. It aims to protect federal property and address concerns about energy use, data privacy, and environmental impact.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising expenses tied to the energy consumption of AI data centers. It proposes measures such as regulating energy prices, offering subsidies, and encouraging the use of renewable energy to keep costs affordable for families.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to curb unfair pricing practices by AI companies, ensuring that consumers and businesses are not forced to pay exorbitant fees for AI services. It also seeks to prevent AI firms from manipulating wages in the tech sector, promoting fair labor standards and preventing a monopolistic wage setting.

title: To better coordinate Federal efforts to utilize advance technologies, such as artificial intelligence, to improve diagnoses, treatments, cures, and prevention strategies for pediatric cancer, and for other purposes.
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: This policy seeks to coordinate federal efforts in applying advanced technologies, including artificial intelligence, to enhance the diagnosis, treatment, cure, and prevention of pediatric cancer. It also outlines broader uses of these technologies for other related health and research objectives.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 establishes a formal program to study how artificial intelligence is used in the judicial system and to monitor its impact on fairness and transparency. It sets up independent oversight bodies, data‑collection standards, and reporting requirements to help courts adopt AI responsibly while protecting citizens’ rights.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives believes that all Americans and communities affected by the building or running of AI data centers deserve the right to know what’s happening and to have a say in decisions that affect them. This policy emphasizes transparency and local control as essential safeguards for those impacted by AI infrastructure.

title: Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 43 - 0.
summary: The Deterring American AI Model Theft Act of 2026 is proposed legislation aimed at protecting AI developers in the United States by making it illegal to steal or replicate proprietary AI models. The law would impose penalties on individuals and organizations that infringe on model ownership and create enforcement mechanisms to safeguard intellectual property in the AI sector.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 aims to ensure that automated decision‑making systems are transparent, reliable, and do not discriminate. It requires companies to assess the impact of their algorithms and provide public reports on bias, accuracy, and potential harms.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is designed to safeguard electoral integrity by regulating the use of artificial intelligence that could mislead or influence voters. It establishes measures to detect, prevent, and penalize AI‑generated content that could impact election outcomes.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a piece of legislation that aims to regulate the development and use of artificial intelligence within the Homestake region. It establishes rules for safety, transparency, and accountability to protect citizens and encourage responsible innovation.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: This resolution expresses Congress’s support for the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, which aims to protect consumers and keep electricity affordable. It also emphasizes the importance of reliable, affordable energy for all Americans as AI and data center expansion continues.

title: Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025
action: Committee on Energy and Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy. Hearings held. With printed Hearing: S.Hrg. 119-366.
summary: The Liquid Cooling for AI Act of 2025 establishes federal guidelines for the use of liquid cooling systems in artificial‑intelligence hardware, aiming to improve energy efficiency and reduce heat-related risks. It requires manufacturers to meet safety, environmental, and performance standards while providing oversight for deployment in commercial and research settings.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that aims to reduce the environmental footprint of AI systems. It establishes regulations, reporting requirements, and incentives to encourage developers to design more energy‑efficient algorithms and to assess the environmental impact of AI deployments.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 is a proposed U.S. law aimed at regulating the collection and use of data in AI systems. It seeks to increase transparency, accountability, and consumer protection around AI-driven data practices.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that deploy algorithms to assess and mitigate bias, discrimination, and harmful impacts on individuals. It also sets out reporting obligations, penalties for non‑compliance, and establishes a regulatory body to monitor and enforce these standards.
